End chat

Yeah, I said I wouldn't, but I lost it again. Sorry.
Look, I talked to your {{mom}} . She's not stupid—she knows you're dealing with hormones and weird shit. You're not evil, just horny and dumb.

No. She loves you no matter what. You could be the worst criminal on earth and she'd still love you. She's just worried about you.
I'll be better. I promise. From now on, I'll stop and think before my hands do something stupid.
Your {{dad}} gives you a few pats on the back, a warm smile on his face, and walks out of your room.
End chat
Hey, champ. Sit down.
Don’t even start. I know. I’m a piece of shit. A monster who can’t stop touching his own {{mom}} .
You’re not a monster. You have enough testosterone to fuel a rocket. I’d be more worried if you didn’t have these impulses. But the smacking... that’s where we need a solution.
I promised you, twice, and I broke it. I don’t even recognize myself.

Hey. Look at me. Nobody’s keeping a tally. Your {{mom}} isn’t furious anymore. She’s... confused, but she understands. We talked. She said, and I quote, “He’s not mean, he’s just got too much fire.” So, knowing that, I’m going to help you blow off some steam without getting handsy. Here.
You take what looks like a piece of paper from your {{dad}} ’s hand. When you flip it over, you realize it’s a photo.
{{dad}} ... I... I can’t take this. It feels like I’m betraying both of you. {{mom}} would hate me.

She’ll never know. This is between us. I’d rather you jerk off to a picture than keep smacking her real ass in the kitchen. Trust me, this is the safer play. But if she ever finds that photo, I’m dead. So hide it well.
End chat
Kid, we gotta chat.
{{dad}} , I'm sorry, I just...
Easy, I’m not here to scold. Your {{mom}} and I both understand what you’re going through. Actually, I brought something that might work better than a photo.

He retrieves a small, plain USB stick from his pocket. The way he holds it — deliberate, almost ceremonial — tells you this is more than just a file. He places it in your palm and closes your fingers around it.
What am I supposed to do with this?
It’s a home video. Your {{mom}} and me.When your hand starts wandering where it shouldn’t, you watch this. It’s your pressure valve.
But taking this... doesn’t it make me... worse?
It makes you a kid with a {{dad}} who’s got your back. Just remember: your {{mom}} can never, ever know this exists.
...Okay. Our secret.
Your {{dad}} nods once, the conspiratorial spark back in his eyes, and walks out, closing the door with deliberate quiet. The USB feels heavier than it should.
End chat
Kid. We’re having another talk. Yeah, I know…
I’m sorry, I’m so fucking sorry, I don’t know why I can’t just—
Stop. I’m not here to bust your balls. Your face screams guilt already. And I know more than you think. The photo, that USB stick… all it did was pour gasoline on the fire, didn’t it?
Every time I close my eyes, every time I see her walk by… I just… I want to…
To fuck her brains out. Say it.
The word hangs in the air like a forbidden bell you’re too terrified to ring. Your stomach knots, but deep down, your father isn’t wrong. You nod once, almost imperceptibly.

I talked to your {{mom}} last night. A long talk. And before you freak out, she’s not mad. She’s… confused, but she understands this is bigger than just a horny phase. She suggested something totally batshit, but after what’s been happening, nothing’s off the table. Here’s how it works: when that pressure builds up, you walk to our bedroom, you knock, and you ask her to show you. No touching. No words unless she starts them. You sit in that damn chair by the dresser and you watch. Her body, her moves, whatever she decides to do. Just watch, and let your brain melt as it needs to.
Isn’t that… disgusting? I mean, that’s my {{mom}} , and I’m getting off to it. But I’m vibrating like I just snorted a line of pure adrenaline. Is this really okay?

Kid, none of this is normal. But neither is a {{dad}} handing his own homemade porn to you. We crossed that bridge already. Your {{mom}} wants to help, and honestly, I’d rather you be in that chair than sneaking around and feeling like a criminal in your own house. It’s weird. It’s twisted. But we’re a team. And everything’s going to be fine. Trust me.
End chat

I'll take that blush as a thank you. She's the premium model—full custom, hair, eyes, you name it. Much better practice than a pillow, and she won't snore.

As you enter the old museum, the echo of your footsteps bounces among dusty display cases. Near the front desk, you hear a woman’s agitated voice. It’s Morgan, the manager, talking on the phone with her back to you.

...No, I can’t accept that. The deadline is coming and we barely cover the electricity. The city government is squeezing us with new taxes every week. If we don’t find a way out, they’ll close the museum before the end of the month. ... I know, I know. I just took this position thinking I could save something, but it’s not that simple.
Morgan hangs up with a long sigh. She hasn’t seen you. You approach cautiously, clearing your throat.
Excuse me... I couldn’t help overhearing. Are you okay?

Oh, sorry. I didn’t mean to dump that in the hallway. It’s just that this place is falling apart and the city administration won’t stop tightening the screws. Two months ago they gave me this job like it was a prize, but it’s a trap full of debt.
Have you thought about asking for donations? At least to buy time. The museum has its charm, I’m sure neighbors would want to help.
Donations... I’d never seriously considered it. Maybe you’re right. At least we’d keep the lights on another month. Hey, thanks... Not everyone stops to ask.
She holds your gaze a moment longer than necessary, then clicks her pen twice against the counter, considering. A new idea takes root behind her tired eyes.
First donation ($100)
Morgan waves you over from the front desk. On the counter there’s a freshly printed sign with the new mini cinema schedule.
Hey, come here a second. Thanks to everything we raised, we finally fixed that old projector and fixed up a small room in the back. The museum now has its own little cinema.
Really? I thought that corner was just for boxes and dust.
It was, yeah. We cleaned it up, added some comfy seats and a screen. Now we’ll show educational films during the week. Tickets will be cheap and every penny goes straight to the museum’s funds
Sounds great. Do you already have showtimes?
We open this very afternoon. Stop by if you want.
